frequency_question: How often does Congress successfully pass a joint resolution of disapproval to block a submitted nuclear cooperation agreement?
membership_rule: Includes all formal 123 agreements submitted for congressional review; excludes informal notifications, non-nuclear trade pacts, or treaties handled under Article II Senate advice and consent rather than statutory nuclear review.

cases.name: U.S.-Iran Sanctions / Related Nuclear Frameworks (Not applicable 123)
Various minor 123 agreements (e.g., Vietnam, South Korea extensions)

provenance_note: claims 30 cases from only 5 named (6.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 30+ named or cataloged major submissions; exact count of minor amendments is higher, none have ever successfully blocked an agreement.
known_gaps: Some minor technical extensions pass silently without active debate, reinforcing the zero-hit rate for successful blockage.
skeleton: Since the statutory framework was established, dozens of peaceful nuclear cooperation agreements (Section 123 agreements) have been submitted to Congress. Zero joint resolutions of disapproval have successfully bypassed or overridden a presidential veto to block an agreement.
multiplier: 0 successful blocks out of approximately 30+ notable submissions over 70 years.
validity_reason: The statutory framework under the Atomic Energy Act remains stable unless Congress amends the underlying statute.
